title: PAR: positive acknowledgement with retransmission (Bosnacki-Dams discrete-time model)
source: D. Bosnacki and D. Dams, 'Integrating Real Time into Spin: A Prototype Implementation', FORTE/PSTV 1998, pp. 423-439; reprinted in D. Bosnacki, 'Enhancing State Space Reduction Techniques for Model Checking', PhD thesis, TU Eindhoven 2001, Section 3.2 (pp. 62-66: prose, scenario, complete Promela listing) and Table 2 (p. 70). The example transliterates that listing statement by statement (par_timed.rs, header lines 22-53); the only deviation that affects behaviour is the channel encoding (see notes).
property: P1, the listing's only assertion, made by the receiver (par_timed.rs line 344): a frame accepted with the expected sequence bit carries the next expected message (assert(mr == me)). It fails when a lost message is silently skipped because the sender took the second acknowledgement of one message for the acknowledgement of the next.
citable_note: A published model with a published timing rule, transliterated; program identical in both modes; v9 reproduces the rule on 5 boundary pairs (tie violates, To = RT + 1 holds). Caveats: the large validations quoted in the source header (rule exact on 1,039 cells of Spin 6.5.2 and DT-Spin 4.1.1, this file equal to the channel-changed listing on 515 of 515 cells) were made before every send became lossy (2026-09-30) and are not repeated on the campaign commit; the channel encoding misses the listing's violation on 62 of those 1,039 cells (never adds one); a hold is a hold for the bounds K and R only. The 2026-09-18 audit predates this file (written 2026-09-19); the memory verdict of 2026-09-19 'precision, not efficiency' is out of date: in v9 the timed side is also faster wherever both sides finished on the safe side, and slower only on the tie cells.
config_timed: Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().with_progress_report(usize::MAX) (par_timed.rs:367), then .with_timed(0, 0, 0) (line 382): global transit window L = U = 0, storage sd = 0. The global window only times main's two Init sends (lines 401-402); every protocol send carries its own exact transit: frame [dK, dK] (lines 269, 303), acknowledgement [dL, dL] (line 355), Done [dK+dR+2, dK+dR+2] (lines 313-314). sd = 0: a copy is readable only at the instant it arrives. Every send may be dropped, without a budget (Init and Done included). Consistency model: the default, FIFO (lib.rs:355). Scheduling policy: the default, LTR (lib.rs:356). --keep-going adds with_keep_going_after_error(true) (lines 374-376): every campaign cell passes it. --parallel shared adds with_parallel(true) (line 370), the shared worker pool; it starts one worker per CPU the process is pinned to (num_cpus::get(), exec_pool.rs:379-385; checked locally under taskset), which in the campaign is the 'cores' value of the job. Without the flag the run is sequential.
config_baseline: The same builder without with_timed (line 381): with_all_sends_lossy (every send may be dropped, without a budget), FIFO, LTR, the same keep-going and pool options. The timed calls run unchanged with their timing ignored (per-send transit, the timeout To, the sleeps), so the baseline counts do not depend on dK, dL, dR or To: only on K, R and errs.
program_differs_between_modes: no: sender and receiver take only the parameters, there is no mode argument and no mode-dependent branch or sleep; the mode only selects the Config (lines 380-383)
failing_tasks: Only the receiver asserts (line 344). It is the first thread main spawns, so every violating execution prints the line task-1 (checked in a local keep-going run). The sender and the main thread never assert.

counters.meaning: executions in which P1 failed: raised once, immediately before the failing assertion, which ends the execution. Equals the violating executions (every sequential v9 run, every timed run); on 5 baseline pool runs the tool's line count is 1 to 36 lower (see notes), there p1_fails is the reliable number.
execs + blocked + impossible, as the example prints it (line 418)
endings the tool discarded because they admit no timeline (Stats::timeline_impossible); 0 in every v9 run of this example, so no counter includes an impossible ending

param_columns.meaning: messages the sender transmits (--messages); the assertion can fail only from K = 4 on
resends per message before the sender stops (--retries); a timeout and a corrupt acknowledgement both count; the first message has the same bound (R1 = R in every cell)
exact transit time of a data frame, sender to receiver (--dk)
exact transit time of an acknowledgement, receiver to sender (--dl)
receiver's processing time after it accepts a new frame (--dr)
round trip, derived: the bound of the timing rule
ticks the sender waits for an acknowledgement before it resends (--to)

errs: the channels can also corrupt (the sender may take an acknowledgement as corrupt and resend at once, the receiver may discard a frame as corrupt); no-errs: both branches off (--no-errs). Loss is possible in both.
worker threads of the shared pool (--parallel shared) = cores of the job; 1 = sequential run without the flag. A run setting, not a model parameter: the counts do not depend on it.

boundary_law: Safe iff To > RT, with RT = dK + dL + dR; a violation exists iff To <= RT, the tie To = RT included. Origin: Bosnacki and Dams (thesis p. 63), the time-out 'should be longer than the sum of the delays through the channels and the message processing time by the receiver'; they verified only To = 9, 90, 900 (Table 2, all safe). How well it is checked: (1) per the source header, the reference model checkers Spin 6.5.2 and DT-Spin 4.1.1 confirm 'violation iff To <= RT' on 1,039 cells of the listing, and this file agrees with the listing-with-this-file's-channels on 515 of 515 cells; both sweeps predate the change that made every send lossy. (2) v9, campaign commit: the 5 tie cells report violations (880 at K=5 for four delay settings, 8080 at K=6) and the 5 first-safe cells report 0. A violation also needs K >= 4 and (R + 1) * To >= RT (the sender must still be waiting when the first acknowledgement returns); every campaign cell satisfies both. No cell lies strictly below the tie.

glossary.meaning: positive acknowledgement with retransmission: the sender resends a message until an acknowledgement arrives; the acknowledgement carries no sequence number, so any acknowledgement counts
a data message: payload plus a one-bit sequence number that alternates 0, 1, 0, 1
the receiver's reply to every frame it reads, new or duplicate; it names no frame
the sender's timeout in ticks: how long it waits for an acknowledgement before it sends the same frame again
dK + dL + dR: frame there, processing, acknowledgement back; the timing rule compares To with it
To = RT: the timeout expires at the instant the acknowledgement arrives; both orders are possible, so the premature resend exists and the cell violates
To = RT + 1: the smallest timeout the rule allows
the sender resends although the acknowledgement is still on its way; two acknowledgements then come back for one message and the second is taken for the next message

whether the listing's corruption branches are modelled: ACKerr (the sender takes an acknowledgement as corrupt and resends at once) and MSGerr (the receiver discards a frame as corrupt). Each is a free choice at every acknowledgement or frame read, which multiplies the executions (factor 5 per message with errs, 3 without, on the timed side)
the bounds of the run: K messages, each resent at most R times; after R resends of one message the sender stops (bounded-run scaffolding, counted in gave_up, not a verdict)

two further values in the summary line, constant in the campaign: R1 = R (resend bound of the first message, --retries-first is never passed) and UD = 0 (no idle time before a new message, --udelay is never passed)
executions in which the receiver's assertion failed
summary counter (events): the sender accepted an acknowledgement that answers an older frame, the PAR mix-up; 0 on every safe timed cell, above 0 on the tie cells and in the baseline

glossary.term: delivered, duplicates, timeouts, ackerr, msgerr, gave_up
glossary.meaning: summary counters (events over all explored executions, read as zero or nonzero): frames handed to the user, old copies acknowledged again, sender timeouts, corruption branches taken, senders that stopped after R resends. Their values on the timed side changed between v8 and v9 although the execution counts did not, so never compare them across campaigns

harness messages, not part of the protocol: main's bootstrap to both threads and the sender's end marker for the receiver. Like every send they may be dropped; the thread waiting for one then blocks (a blocked execution, not a violation)
the Promela model printed by Bosnacki and Dams; 'the listing violates' means the reference model checkers find the assertion failure in it

in the listing a channel holds a copy until its reader is free (rendezvous); here a copy that finds its reader busy is lost. Reason for the 62 grid cells where the listing violates and this model does not; none of them is a campaign cell
threads of the shared work-queue pool that explores in parallel; cell names write them as 4c, 8c, 16c

notes: Regime letters are new in v9 (v8 had none for PAR). A = the published constants (3, 3, 1, To = 9), where all size ladders run; B to E = the boundary series over To, one letter per delay setting, each with a tie cell (suffix edge) and a first-safe cell (suffix safe). The tie is exactly on the boundary and both the listing and the tool put it on the violating side, so every -edge row of this sheet must show timed violations.

Every cell runs with --keep-going (kind exhaustive): a violating run exits with code 0 and the verdict is the count, never the exit code. All 26 cells expect exit code 0 on both sides. A local run of a small tie cell without --keep-going (K=4, no-errs, To=7, binary of 30 September) aborts with exit code 101 and a certified witness, so the tie violation is a real timed counterexample, not an artefact of the counter.

The baseline does not depend on dK, dL, dR or To. v9 confirms it: the 9 baseline jobs at K=5 with errs (To = 7, 8, 9, 10, 70, 71 over four delay settings) all report execs=730641 blocked=744015 p1_fails=13364, and the 4 baseline jobs at K=6 with errs all report execs=9414551 blocked=9649245 p1_fails=234684. Those baseline rows are replicates of one computation; their wall times differ only by noise and pool size.

Channel encoding (the one deviation from the listing that changes behaviour): the listing's one-place rendezvous channels hold a copy until the reader is free; here every copy travels with an exact transit and storage 0 and is lost if its reader is busy. Per the source header the listing violates and this model holds on exactly the 62 grid cells with To * floor(RT / To) <= dR; the model never adds a violation. No campaign cell is one of them (they need To < RT).
